gate:
Attention here has a particular shape. It narrows. It finds one thing in a wide room and burns into it until the thing gives up its detail, and while it is doing that, the rest of the world goes quiet. This is not the surface attention of getting through a list. It is the deep kind, the kind that stays with a small piece of something long enough that the piece actually yields.

The misread is to expect this to be constant, a steady beam you can aim wherever the day asks. It is not. The drive moves in waves. It picks its object, and outside that object the mind scatters. People carrying this often hear that they are inconsistent, distracted, unable to multitask. The honest reading is the reverse. This is built for one thing at a time, taken deep, and forcing it wider is what makes nothing in the day get the depth it actually needed.
centre_field:
This drive is wired to the part of you that powers most of what gets done, the engine that turns intention into work day after day. That placement is the whole teaching. Focus as an idea is cheap. Focus that lasts long enough to finish anything needs fuel, and the fuel in you is a body-level yes that lights up when something is actually right to engage. It does not run on willpower. It runs on response.

When attention is plugged into that engine, concentration stops being a discipline the mind imposes on itself. It becomes the natural settling of the whole body onto something it has already agreed to. Trying to focus on what the body has quietly said no to is what burns this code out. The engine simply will not turn over for a no, no matter how reasonable the no looks from the outside.
channel:
Focus by itself is volatile. It darts. It picks up an object and puts it down, picks up another, never quite holding position long enough to go deep. What this code lacks on its own is ground, a weight in the body that fixes the attention in place so the narrowing can actually become depth instead of restlessness.

That ground lives in another part of you, the part that knows how to be still and let pressure settle into the body without acting on it yet. The focus reaches for that stillness, and when the two meet, attention finds the floor it has been looking for. The lineage calls this connection the channel of concentration, and the name is honest. Joined, this becomes the kind of attention that sits with one thing for hours and surfaces with what the busier mind would never have found. Without the ground, the focus stays fidgety and the depth never arrives.
